cases.sentence: Это была ___ возвышенная, таинственная, связанная с рядом прекрасных мыслей и чувств.
cases.translation: This was an elevated, mysterious religion, connected with a whole series of beautiful thoughts and feelings.
cases.explain: Религия is a predicate noun after the linking verb была (was), so it takes the nominative case.

cases.sentence: Она упомянула, что для ___ к нам Христа нет ничтожных горестей.
cases.translation: She mentioned that for Christ's compassion toward us, no sorrow is insignificant.
cases.explain: The preposition для (for) always governs the genitive case.

cases.sentence: Опять и опять перебирала она в своем воспоминании все отношения свои к этому ___.
cases.translation: Again and again she went over in her memory all her relations to this family.
cases.explain: The preposition к (toward) governs the dative case.

cases.sentence: Когда она застала у нее католического ___, мадам Шталь старательно держала свое лицо в тени абажура.
cases.translation: When she once found a Catholic priest with her, Madame Stahl carefully kept her face in the shadow of the lampshade.
cases.explain: Священника is the direct object of застала (found), and as an animate masculine noun its accusative form matches the genitive.

cases.sentence: Она третьего дня с ___ сказала: «Вот, все дожидался вас, не хотел без вас пить кофе».
cases.translation: The other day she said with vexation: 'There, he kept waiting for you, wouldn't drink coffee without you.'
cases.explain: The preposition с (with) governs the instrumental case, expressing manner.

cases.sentence: Она только думала в душе, что нельзя говорить об излишестве в ___ христианства.
cases.translation: She thought to herself that one could not speak of excess in the matter of Christianity.
cases.explain: The preposition в (in) governs the prepositional case here.

reading.ru: Китти познакомилась и с госпожою Шталь, и знакомство это вместе с дружбой к Вареньке не только имело на нее сильное влияние, но утешало ее в ее горе.
reading.question: What effect did Kitty's acquaintance with Madame Stahl and friendship with Varenka have on her?
options: It had a strong influence on her and comforted her in her grief
It made her indifferent to religion
It caused her to quarrel with her mother immediately
It made her leave the spa
reading.correct: It had a strong influence on her and comforted her in her grief
reading.explain: The text says the acquaintance had a strong influence on Kitty and comforted her in her grief.

reading.ru: Ей открылось то, что кроме жизни инстинктивной, которой до сих пор отдавалась Китти, была жизнь духовная.
reading.question: How did the new spiritual religion Kitty discovered differ from the religion she knew from childhood?
options: It had nothing in common with the childhood religion of church services and memorized Slavonic texts
It was identical to her childhood religion
It rejected the existence of God
It was taught to her by her mother
reading.correct: It had nothing in common with the childhood religion of church services and memorized Slavonic texts
reading.explain: The text describes this new religion as having nothing in common with the one she knew from childhood, of church services and memorized Slavonic texts.

reading.ru: Мадам Шталь говорила с Китти как с милым ребенком, на которого любуешься, как на воспоминания своей молодости, и только один раз упомянула о том, что во всех людских горестях утешение дает лишь любовь и вера, и что для сострадания к нам Христа нет ничтожных горестей, и тотчас же перевела разговор на другое.
reading.question: How did Madame Stahl speak to Kitty?
options: As if to a dear child, and only once mentioned that love and faith comfort every grief
She never spoke to Kitty directly
reading.correct: As if to a dear child, and only once mentioned that love and faith comfort every grief
reading.explain: The text says Madame Stahl spoke to Kitty as to a dear child, and mentioned once that love and faith give comfort in every grief.

reading.ru: Она заметила, что, расспрашивая про ее родных, мадам Шталь улыбнулась презрительно, что было противно христианской доброте.
reading.question: What troubling thing did Kitty notice about Madame Stahl?
options: She smiled contemptuously when asked about her relatives, which was contrary to Christian kindness
She wept whenever her family was mentioned
She was always angry at Varenka
reading.correct: She smiled contemptuously when asked about her relatives, which was contrary to Christian kindness
reading.explain: Kitty noticed Madame Stahl smiled contemptuously when asked about her relatives, contrary to Christian kindness.

reading.ru: Но зато Варенька, одинокая, без родных, без друзей, с грустным разочарованием, ничего не желавшая, ничего не жалевшая, была тем самым совершенством, о котором только позволяла себе мечтать Китти.
reading.question: What did Kitty see in Varenka?
options: The very perfection Kitty had only allowed herself to dream of
Someone Kitty envied for her wealth
A rival for Madame Stahl's affection
reading.correct: The very perfection Kitty had only allowed herself to dream of
reading.explain: The text says Varenka was exactly the perfection Kitty had only permitted herself to dream about.

reading.ru: По рассказам Вареньки о том, что делала мадам Шталь и другие, кого она называла, Китти уже составила себе счастливый план будущей жизни.
reading.question: What did Kitty do based on Varenka's stories about Madame Stahl and others?
options: She formed a happy plan for her future life
She wrote a letter to her mother about it
reading.correct: She formed a happy plan for her future life
reading.explain: From Varenka's stories, Kitty had already composed a happy plan for her future life.

reading.ru: Но все это были тайные мечты, которые Китти не высказывала ни матери, ни Вареньке.
reading.question: Did Kitty share her plans with her mother or Varenka?
options: No, these were secret dreams she told no one
Yes, she told her mother everything
reading.correct: No, these were secret dreams she told no one
reading.explain: The text says these were secret dreams Kitty confided to neither her mother nor Varenka.

reading.ru: Сначала княгиня замечала только, что Китти находится под сильным влиянием своего онгумо, как она называла госпоже Шталь и в особенности к Вареньке.
reading.question: What did the princess (Kitty's mother) first notice?
options: That Kitty was strongly influenced by her infatuation with Madame Stahl and especially Varenka
That Kitty wanted to leave the spa
reading.correct: That Kitty was strongly influenced by her infatuation with Madame Stahl and especially Varenka
reading.explain: The princess first noticed only that Kitty was under the strong influence of her infatuation with Madame Stahl and Varenka.

reading.ru: Китти, очевидно, гордилась тем, что исполняла в этом семействе обязанности сестры Милосердия.
reading.question: What was Kitty visibly proud of?
options: Performing the duties of a sister of mercy for the Petrov family
reading.correct: Performing the duties of a sister of mercy for the Petrov family
reading.explain: Kitty was evidently proud that she performed the duties of a sister of mercy in that family.

reading.ru: «Никогда ни в чем не следует впадать в крайность», — говорила она ей.
reading.question: What warning did the princess give Kitty?
options: Never to fall into extremes in anything
Never to speak with Madame Stahl again
reading.correct: Never to fall into extremes in anything
reading.explain: The princess told her: 'One should never fall into extremes in anything.'

reading.ru: Она таила их не потому, чтобы она не уважала, не любила свою мать, но только потому, что это была ее мать.
reading.question: Why did Kitty hide her new thoughts and feelings from her mother?
options: Simply because she was her mother, not from lack of love or respect
Because her mother had forbidden such talk
Because she planned to run away
reading.correct: Simply because she was her mother, not from lack of love or respect
reading.explain: The text says she hid them not because she didn't respect or love her mother, but only because she was her mother.

reading.ru: «Что же, поезжайте», — отвечала княгиня, вглядываясь в смущенное лицо дочери и стараясь угадать причину ее смущения.
reading.question: How did the princess react when Kitty answered about the planned outing?
options: She agreed but studied her daughter's embarrassed face, trying to guess the reason for her confusion
reading.correct: She agreed but studied her daughter's embarrassed face, trying to guess the reason for her confusion
reading.explain: The princess answered 'Well, go then,' while peering into her daughter's embarrassed face to guess the cause.

reading.ru: Она не знала причины перемена к себе Анны Павловны, но догадывалась.
reading.question: Did Kitty know the reason for Anna Pavlovna's change toward her?
options: She did not know for certain, but she suspected
She knew exactly and explained it to her mother
She was told directly by Petrov
reading.correct: She did not know for certain, but she suspected
reading.explain: The text says she did not know the reason for the change in Anna Pavlovna toward her, but she guessed.

reading.ru: Она вспоминала наивную радость, выражавшуюся на круглом добродушном лице Анны Павловны при их встречах, вспоминала их тайные переговоры о больном, заговоры о том, чтобы отвлечь его от работы, которая была ему запрещена, и увезти его гулять, привязанность меньшого мальчика, называвшего ее «моя Китти», не хотевшего без нее ложиться спать.
reading.question: What did Kitty recall about her earlier relationship with the Petrov family?
options: Anna Pavlovna's naive joy at their meetings and the youngest boy's attachment to her
Anna Pavlovna's jealousy from the very start
reading.correct: Anna Pavlovna's naive joy at their meetings and the youngest boy's attachment to her
reading.explain: She recalled Anna Pavlovna's naive joy at their meetings and the youngest boy's attachment, not wanting to go to bed without her.

reading.question: How does Kitty recall the earlier days with the Petrov family?
options: As painful and awkward from the start
reading.explain: The text repeats 'Как все это было хорошо!' (How good all this had been!).

reading.ru: Анна Павловна притворно встречала Китти и, не переставая, наблюдала ее и мужа.
reading.question: How did Anna Pavlovna's behavior change toward Kitty recently?
options: She greeted Kitty with false friendliness while constantly watching her and her husband
She stopped speaking to Kitty entirely
She invited Kitty to live with them
reading.correct: She greeted Kitty with false friendliness while constantly watching her and her husband
reading.explain: The text says Anna Pavlovna met Kitty with pretended warmth while constantly observing her and her husband.

reading.ru: Все это так просто, но он так неловко это принял, так долго благодарил, что и мне стало неловко».
reading.question: What made Kitty feel awkward regarding Petrov?
options: He accepted a simple gesture so awkwardly and thanked her so long that she too felt uncomfortable
He refused to speak to her
reading.correct: He accepted a simple gesture so awkwardly and thanked her so long that she too felt uncomfortable
reading.explain: The text describes Petrov accepting a plaid so awkwardly and thanking her so long that it made her uncomfortable too.

reading.ru: Он так жалок, говорила она себе вслед за этим.
reading.question: What did Kitty tell herself about Petrov, right after doubting the possibility of his feelings?
options: That he was indifferent to her
reading.explain: The text says she told herself afterward, 'He is so pitiful.'
